milestone: OAuth smart consumer — a strongly-recommended, token-less, cross-platform SessionStart recall+capture hook (operator-installed)
installation: The OPERATOR (human) merges `snippet.hooks` into their settings.json `hooks` key — an agent cannot do it: merging an externally-sourced hook into settings.json is self-modification with external content, which Claude Code's safety classifier blocks. No script file, no token, no placeholders.
policy: Claude Code connects over OAuth (no static token). The MCP `instructions` field is a passive nudge the model may ignore (claude.ai, on-demand by design, does); this SessionStart hook is what makes recall + capture fire RELIABLY at the start of every session — without it Claude Code may not auto-recall or auto-capture at all, so it is strongly recommended, not optional. It is a TOKEN-LESS `command` hook that writes a fixed reminder to stdout — for SessionStart, stdout is added to the model's context directly (no JSON envelope needed) — telling the model to LOAD THE SKILLS (skill_fetch `core`, then its dispatcher), call smart_bootstrap, and recall. The skill-loading clause is load-bearing and must stay first: the hook is the only instruction some sessions read, so a hook that merely *cites* the skills produces a session that never fetches them — it bootstraps, recalls, and then silently skips every capture rule the skills carry (observed 2026-07-26). What the hook must NOT carry is a one-shot procedure: onboarding a project happens once per project and was costing every session its space (roadmap 51c). It keeps only the clause that makes the server's answer useful — pass the derived project_id — because the smart_bootstrap call is instructed here, and an argument-less call cannot be told that this project has no memory. It holds no secret and calls nothing on the server: the recall is the model's own tool call, so its results land in context naturally. Per-prompt recall stays model-driven (hook inputs can't be templated with the prompt). Cross-platform: a single-quoted `echo` runs identically under every shell Claude Code uses for hooks — `sh` on macOS/Linux, Git Bash or PowerShell on Windows (single quotes are string delimiters in all three; Claude Code does not use cmd.exe for hooks). It avoids `printf` (absent on Windows) and the JSON envelope.

smart_bootstrap.note: The model calls it itself at session start (nudged by this hook + the skill). Surfaces the smart consumer's owned wikis — its operational wiki (marked is_self: true) + any project wikis — and pending briefing items. Inside a project the model passes the derived project_id and the response carries first_connect: whether this project already has a wiki, and when it has none, the one line pointing at the smart-onboarding skill. That is why the hook no longer describes onboarding itself — the server volunteers the trigger, so the procedure does not have to be read by every session for a thing that happens once per project. Smart-only. See wiki/protocol/tool-reference.md.

recall_core_global.note: The model calls it on the first prompt / on a topic shift (steered by the skill). Owner-scoped transversal recall over the user's own wikis. Smart-only.

wiki_admin_push.note: Day-to-day single-page edits are pushed normally; its response carries signpost_hint and warnings[] (pages whose blocks are too dense to section cleanly). The one-shot BULK copy of a pre-existing wiki runs in a script (PowerShell/curl) that walks the tree and calls wiki_admin_push over /mcp — the bytes go file->script->server, never through the model context. That procedure lives in the smart-onboarding skill, not in this hook.

hooks.command: echo 'mwe-mcp memory is connected. This line is a nudge, not the contract — the skills are. Load them now: skill_fetch the core skill and follow its bootstrap dispatcher, which tells you which further skills to load (smart-consumer / smart-codebase inside a project, core-globalmemory outside one). Also call smart_bootstrap to pull your operational wiki and any briefing, and recall relevant memory before answering. Inside a project pass the project_id core tells you how to derive: the response says whether this project already has memory, and what to do when it does not. Capture durable facts as you go, routed per those skills: project knowledge to the project wiki, your own operating notes to your operational wiki (including the dated entry in its conversations.md), facts about the user via wiki_ingest_message. Never dump everything into the user standard memory.'
